subject: Re: US privacy addendum — telemetry isolation & onshore fallback
messages:
From: Alex Murray <amurray@greenhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@greenhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines — US privacy addendum (telemetry / subprocessors)

Jonas,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached are GreenHealth's redlines to the US privacy addendum (PDF attached). Two quick asks up front so we can move this through procurement: 

1) Service provider / sale classification language — we need clear confirmation that Redwood will act only as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and the other applicable state laws in the addendum. The redlines include a short definition we prefer; please confirm whether Redwood accepts that or propose alternative wording.

2) Telemetry / aggregated logs — we are asking for an isolation carve-out: telemetry used for observability must be aggregated, non-identifiable, and not used to reconstruct customer data flows. See comments on p.4 of the PDF. We also want to understand the onshore fallback plan for subpoenas/requests involving telemetry.

If you can punt these two bullets in a short reply I'll share the file with procurement and legal here. We also flagged a specific subprocessor (CloudOps SaaS) on p.6 — we'd appreciate visibility on whether that vendor supports an onshore-only failover.

Attachments: GreenHealth_DPA_Redlines_v2.pdf (redlines, comments)

Alex Murray
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
GreenHealth Systems

--

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — US privacy addendum (telemetry / subprocessors)

Alex — thanks for the detailed redlines and for surfacing the telemetry carve-out. Looping in Marissa (privacy), Aditya (product infra), and Laura (legal ops) so we can respond with specifics.

Short answers to your two asks: 
- Service provider role: Redwood is prepared to accept service-provider / processor language consistent with CCPA/CPRA obligations for the scope of the addendum. We have a proposed clause that mirrors your suggested definition but adds a limited forwarding clause for security/defense reasons (we'll put wording in the attached response).
- Telemetry: high-level commitment — telemetry we retain for operational health is aggregated by default and subject to the data minimization rules in our internal telemetry policy. We cannot commit to permanent onshore-only retention for all telemetry because some customers run in multi-region deployments, but we can offer an onshore fallback arrangement for telemetry tied to regulated workloads (contractually scoped).

Aditya — can you confirm the technical approach for onshore failover for CloudOps SaaS (the subprocessor called out by GreenHealth) and whether we can provide proof of segregation for telemetry buckets?

Laura — can you review the attached draft response and the limited forwarding carve-out for security incidents? We're aiming to get this back to GreenHealth by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood_Response_DPA_v1.pdf (draft)

Thanks,

Thanks Jonas — that helps. Two follow-ups from our side after reviewing the attached response PDF: 

- The limited forwarding carve-out for security is understandable, but GreenHealth needs a narrow notification window (48 hours) for any compelled disclosure unless prohibited by law. Can Redwood accept a notice-when-possible clause with a 48-hour target?
- For the onshore fallback, procurement wants either (A) an onshore-only telemetry retention profile for regulated accounts, or (B) proof of written contract terms with the CloudOps subprocessor that require onshore fallback within 24 hours of notice. Option A is preferred but we recognize it implies additional cost; option B is acceptable if you can provide the written commitment.

Also — procurement has requested SOC2 evidence for the telemetry pipeline controls and a short inventory of subprocessors with their region controls. Can you provide that as attachments when you send the updated addendum?

We'd like to keep this moving; if possible, we'll aim to route the updated addendum back through our procurement by Friday.

Alex

Alex — thanks for the feedback and the timeline. Quick summary of what we can deliver and next steps: 

1) Notice for compelled disclosures: Redwood can agree to notify GreenHealth "when legally permitted" and will treat "48 hours" as our internal SLA target when notice is not prohibited. We put the clause into the attached redline and highlighted the language that binds us to a 48-hour target except where law bars notification.

2) Onshore fallback for telemetry: we offer two paths (both contractually available):
   - Onshore retention profile (Option A): for regulated workloads Redwood can enforce an onshore-only telemetry retention profile — this requires a dedicated ingestion path and an ops runbook, and will be priced as an add-on.
   - Subprocessor-written commitment (Option B): we can obtain a contractual written commitment from CloudOps SaaS to perform onshore failover within 24 hours of notice and provide that contract excerpt as evidence.

3) Evidence package: attached SOC 2 letter (summary) and a current subprocessor inventory with region annotations. We redacted internal vendor phone numbers.

4) Next mechanics: I've attached a DocuSign link for the redline (we accepted most of your baseline edits and kept a short security-forwarding carve-out). If you'd prefer Option A, Jonas and I can produce a priced amendment and run the internal approval loop.

Attachments: Redwood_Response_DPA_v1.pdf (updated with 48-hour notice), SOC2_Summary_Telemetry.pdf, Subprocessor_Inventory_202704.json (inventory stub), Docusign_Link.txt

If that package looks good, please return the DocuSign and we'll move to procurement. If you want the CloudOps contract excerpt instead, let us know and we'll pull it from legal ops.
